newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-S.AFRICA NAME 15-STRONG SQUAD FOR PAKISTAN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-S.AFRICA NAME 15-STRONG SQUAD FOR PAKISTAN.

text.p: The United Cricket Board of South Africa (UCBSA) on Thursday announced a 15-strong squad for the three-test tour of Pakistan in October.
Opening pair Gary Kirsten and Andrew Hudson have both been included, despite being dropped during the 2-1 home series defeat by Australia.
The most notable omission is Western Province batsman Herschelle Gibbs.

"Herschelle is not out of the reckoning and I maintain that he will become a significant force in test cricket, but Pakistan is a tour which calls for experience and Kirsten and Hudson provide that," selectors' convenor Peter Pollock said.

The squad had been selected with the tests in mind and that for the one-day matches at the end of the tour, specialists will be flown in, with the likes of Allan Donald and Brett Schultz going home early to rest ahead of the tour to Australia which follows a fortnight later.
That opens the door for Gibbs, all-rounder Derek Crookes and paceman Rudi Bryson, who all played in the seven-match one-day series against Australia.
Western Province all-rounder Brian McMillan, who missed the one day games against Australia with a bruised heel, is being asked to fill the problem number three position in the batting order.

"Mac's bowling is a bit of a bonus at this stage of his career and we might well ask Western Province to bat him at number three next season. He's a very important member of the squad and we don't want to throw his competitiveness and exerience away too soon," Pollock said.

Squad: Hansie Cronje (captain), Gary Kirsten, Adam Bacher, Andrew Hudson, Brian McMillan, Daryll Cullinan, Jacques Kallis, Jonty Rhodes, Shaun Pollock, Dave Richardson, Pat Symcox, Paul Adams, Allan Donald, Lance Klusener, Brett Schultz.
